hu-1skP.title: Google car: rare white Gen 4
hu-1skP.summary: A white newer-generation car (Gen 4) can rarely be found. It also exists in other European countries.

hu-1y8d.title: Phone numbers: 8 or 10 digits, area code inside
hu-1y8d.summary: Numbers have 8 or 10 digits. The area code is the first two digits (8-digit numbers) or the third and fourth (10-digit ones). The capital's code is just a single 1. Area codes with a second digit of 0 or 1 are not tied to a region.

hu-3LxD.title: Sign: street names ending in -utca or -út
hu-3LxD.summary: Street names usually end in "utca", and bigger roads use "út". Both words mean street and exist only in this language.

hu-8FCa.title: Sign: blue or green arrow street signs on poles
hu-8FCa.summary: Blue or green arrow-shaped street signs attached to utility poles or street lights suggest the far northeast county. Blue arrow signs near the capital in the north are on blue posts.

hu-94Xz.title: Houses: light stone, red tiled roofs
hu-94Xz.summary: Stone houses in light colours, almost always with red tiled roofs. Suburban houses are mostly one storey, central ones can be taller. Town centres are old but well kept.

hu-A2Fx.title: Plate: long white, yellow for taxis
hu-A2Fx.summary: Long white EU-style plates. Taxis have yellow plates, newer electric cars green ones. Since July 2022 the new format includes the coat of arms.

hu-Ad5o.title: Landscape: flat southeast
hu-Ad5o.summary: The southeast is extremely flat with hardly any hills. The north and west are forested hills and mountains, tallest in the north and lower in the southwest.

hu-C5sq.title: Landscape: big lake, hotels, hilly shore
hu-C5sq.summary: The only large lake visible in Street View. The shores are moderately hilly, fairly built-up tourist areas with many more small hotels than almost anywhere else.

hu-GR8q.title: Google car: grey, dead winter look (Gen 3)
hu-GR8q.summary: Most older Gen 3 coverage was taken in winter, so it looks grey and lifeless. Czechia and Bulgaria have the same look.

hu-N7yw.title: Sign: posts taller than the camera
hu-N7yw.summary: Sign posts often look very tall, frequently taller than the Street View camera.

hu-NJDC.title: Road lines: white, yellow on bike lanes
hu-NJDC.summary: Road lines are all white, except bicycle lane lines, which are usually yellow.

hu-PvaK.title: Bollard: black-white wedge, red reflector
hu-PvaK.summary: A black and white wedge-shaped bollard with a red reflector at the front and a white one at the back. Blue reflectors are also fairly common.

differs.how: Croatian reflector sits higher up and the bollard looks thinner

hu-Tbty.title: Sign: pedestrian crossing, five stripes
hu-Tbty.summary: A five-stripe crossing sign with a person wearing a belt set noticeably low, as if sagging his trousers. A rarer type has four stripes and a person holding a bag. Croatia and Slovakia also have five stripes and a belt.

hu-Vhaj.title: Chevron: white on red
hu-Vhaj.summary: White arrows on a red background. Black-and-white chevrons also appear but are much less common.

hu-XwNR.title: Sign: green direction signs, blue on M roads
hu-XwNR.summary: Most direction signs are green with a white inner border. Those on M-numbered highways are blue.

hu-ZEB9.title: Landscape: snowy road, bollards
hu-ZEB9.summary: The road east of Tornanadaska, next to the Slovakian border, stands out by snow on and beside the road, bollards, and a railway running right next to it.

hu-bxAw.title: Sign: four bolts in a tall rectangle
hu-bxAw.summary: Signs are bolted to the post with four bolts forming a tall rectangle. This is not common in other Eastern European countries.

hu-d5CC.title: Landscape: barren wet natural grassland
hu-d5CC.summary: Unlike the mostly farmed plains, this area around a national park is barren and wet, natural grassland.

hu-dM2y.title: Pole: concrete with thin holes down to the
hu-dM2y.summary: The most common pole is concrete with a row of thin holes running all the way to the ground. Wooden poles are also fairly common.

differs.how: Polish holey poles have no holes near the ground and are thinner
Romanian holes are much wider or much taller

hu-eBWy.title: Road: green kilometre markers
hu-eBWy.summary: Green kilometre markers stand along most roads. On highways, the numbers match the small yellow boxes near exits on the map.

hu-g7PT.title: Language: long words, double acute accents
hu-g7PT.summary: A very distinct look with many acute accents, umlauts over o and u, and long words. The letters Ő and Ű with double accents only exist in this language. It is also spoken in central Romania and southern Slovakia.

differs.how: Hungarian is also spoken in central Romania
Hungarian is also spoken in southern Slovakia

hu-gMof.title: Sign: unique street signs in big towns
hu-gMof.summary: An infographic of ten large towns whose street signs look unique, and what makes each one different.

hu-jEV4.title: Google car: small grey flag on antenna
hu-jEV4.summary: On older Gen 3 cars (blurrier, softer colours) a small grey flag on the antenna is fairly common. Czechia, Slovakia, Romania and Bulgaria have it too.

hu-ktc7.title: Road numbers: first digit circles the capital
hu-ktc7.summary: The first digit of numbered roads is arranged in a circle around the capital, so learning that pattern lets you place any numbered road.

hu-lm-740386.title: Sign: district in Roman numerals plus Kerület
hu-lm-740386.summary: In the capital, street signs show a district number in Roman numerals followed by "Kerület".

hu-lm-740388.title: Sign: street name with big diagonal corners
hu-lm-740388.summary: In Győr, street signs have large diagonal corners.

hu-lm-741737.title: Sign: blue text, angular corners
hu-lm-741737.summary: In Kecskemét, street signs have blue text and angular corners.

hu-s2B8.title: Sign: road numbers in shields, green or blue M
hu-s2B8.summary: Besides European roads, numbered roads have green signs, and highways starting with M have blue signs. The number sits in a small shield shape.

hu-s76v.title: Google car: black Gen 4, never an antenna
hu-s76v.summary: A black newer-generation car (Gen 4) that never has an antenna. Black cars exist in many European countries, but they usually show an antenna.

hu-xpQW.title: Sign: street names in a thick metal frame
hu-xpQW.summary: A street sign in a thick metal frame points to the western part of the country.

hu-zgXE.title: Town names: local prefixes (infographic)
hu-zgXE.summary: Many town names begin with a local prefix that points to a region. Study the infographic for the most common ones; a few exceptions exist.
